{{short description|Awarded every year by the American Mathematical Society}}
The '''Leroy P. Steele Prizes''' are awarded every year since 1970 by the [[American Mathematical Society]] for distinguished research work and writing in the field of [[mathematics]]. Since 1993, the awards have been split into three categories: lifetime achievement, mathematical exposition, and research.

The prizes were begun from a bequest of [[Leroy P. Steele]] and were set up in honor of [[George David Birkhoff]], [[William Fogg Osgood]] and [[William Caspar Graustein]]. The way the prizes are awarded was changed in 1976 and 1993, but the initial aim of honoring expository writing as well as research has been retained. The prizes—$10,000 for lifetime achievement,<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement (1993 - present) |url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=25 |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref> and $5,000   for mathematical exposition<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Leroy P. Steele Prize for Mathematical Exposition (1993 - present) |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=26 |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref> and for research<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research (1993 - present) |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=27 |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref>—are not given on a strict national basis, but relate to writing in English (originally, or in translation) and mathematical activity in the United States.

| [[Deane Montgomery]]
| for his lasting impact on mathematics, particularly mathematics in America. He is one of the founders of the modern theory of transformation groups and is particularly known for his contributions to the solution of [[Hilbert's fifth problem]].

| rowspan=3 | 1987
| [[Martin Gardner]]
| for his many books and articles on mathematics and particularly for his column "Mathematical Games" in ''[[Scientific American]]''.
|-
| [[Herbert Federer]] and [[Wendell Fleming]]
| for their pioneering paper "Normal and integral currents".<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Federer | first1=Herbert | last2=Fleming | first2=Wendell H. | title=Normal and integral currents | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=72 | issue=3 | date=1960 | doi=10.2307/1970227 | url= | access-date=| url-access= |pages=458–520 | jstor=1970227 }}</ref>
|-
| [[Samuel Eilenberg]]
| for his fundamental contributions to topology and algebra, in particular for his classic papers on singular homology and his work on axiomatic homology theory which had a profound influence on the development of algebraic topology.
|-
| rowspan=3 | 1986
| [[Donald E. Knuth]]
| for his expository work, [[The Art of Computer Programming]], 3 Volumes (1st Edition 1968, 2nd Edition 1973).
|-
| [[Rudolf E. Kálmán]]
| for his two fundamental papers, "A new approach to linear filtering and prediction problems"<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kálmán | first=R. Bucy).
|-
| [[Saunders Mac Lane]]
| for his many contributions to algebra and algebraic topology, and in particular for his pioneering work in homological and categorical algebra.
|-
| rowspan=3 | 1985
| [[Michael Spivak]]
| for his five-volume set, "A Comprehensive Introduction to Differential Geometry" (second edition, Publish or Perish, 1979).
|-
| [[Robert Steinberg]]
| for three papers on various aspects of the theory of algebraic groups: "Representations of algebraic groups",<ref>{{cite journal | last=Steinberg | first=Robert | title=Representations of algebraic groups | journal=Nagoya Mathematical Journal | volume=22 | date=1963 | issn=0027-7630 | doi=10.1017/S0027763000011016 | doi-access= | pages=33–56 | url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/02AE5498AF62BCAB6B313C75016E6015/S0027763000011016a.pdf/representations-of-algebraic-groups.pdf | access-date=}}</ref> "Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups",<ref>{{cite journal | last=Steinberg | first=Robert | title=Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups | journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS | volume=25 | issue= | date=1965 | issn= | doi=10.1007/BF02684397 | pages=49–80 | url=https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/BF02684397.pdf | access-date=| url-access= |zbl=0136.30002|mr=0180554}}</ref> and ''Endomorphisms of Linear Algebraic Groups''.<ref>{{cite book | last=Steinberg | first=Robert | title=Endomorphisms of Linear Algebraic Groups | publisher=American Mathematical Society | publication-place=Providence | edition= | isbn=9780821812808|year=1968|series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society|volume=80}}</ref>
|-
| [[Hassler Whitney]]
| for his fundamental work on geometric problems, particularly in the general theory of manifolds, in the study of differentiable functions on closed sets, in geometric integration theory, and in the geometry of the tangents to a singular analytic space.
|-
| rowspan=3 | 1984
| [[Elias M. Stein]]
| for his book ''Singular Integrals and the Differentiability Properties of Functions''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Stein |first=Elias M. |title=Singular Integrals and Differentiability Properties of Functions |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=1970 |isbn=0-691-08079-8 |series=Princeton Mathematical Series}}</ref>
|-
| [[Lennart Carleson]]
| for his papers "An interpolation problem for bounded analytic functions",<ref>{{cite journal | last=Carleson | first=Lennart | title=An interpolation problem for bounded analytic functions | journal=American Journal of Mathematics | volume=80 | issue=4 | date=1958 | doi=10.2307/2372840 | pages=921–930 | jstor=2372840 | url= | access-date=| url-access= }}</ref> "Interpolation by bounded analytic functions and the Corona problem",<ref>{{cite journal | last=Carleson | first=Lennart | title=Interpolations by bounded analytic functions and the Corona problem | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=76 | issue=3 | date=1962 | doi=10.2307/1970375 | pages=547–559 | jstor=1970375 | url= | access-date=| url-access= }}</ref> and "On convergence and growth of partial sums of Fourier series".<ref>{{cite journal | last=Carleson | first=Lennart | title=On convergence and growth of partial sums of Fourier series | journal=Acta Mathematica | volume=116 | issue= | date=1966 | issn=0001-5962 | doi=10.1007/BF02392815 | doi-access= | pages=135–157 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/acta-mathematica/volume-116/issue-none/On-convergence-and-growth-of-partial-sums-of-Fourier-series/10.1007/BF02392815.pdf | access-date=}}</ref>
|-
| [[Joseph L. Doob]]
